records.source_body:
## Post-merge recovery after #507

Fix the source-licence false claim in the iOS pilot README, synchronize generated handoff count with 516 actual test files, and reconcile P1 transaction-only policy/dedup replay with the previously merged service-role hardening migration. No production migrations or bypasses.

**Requires** exact-head full tests and strict native PostgreSQL replay. Remaining cross-browser anomalies are under diagnosis and will be repaired here, not ignored. Not an authorization to deploy.

All failing required checks must turn green before merge. GitHub main branch protection and independent production environment review remain external governance requirements.

## October 8 — Cross-browser bounded media startup and cancellation repair

**Root cause from exact-head GitHub job logs**
- WebKit (4 cases): synthetic camera playback left `HTMLMediaElement.play()` pending indefinitely. Camera UI did not surface a preview or supported fallback within 12 seconds.
- Firefox (1 case): the 20 × 20 pixel CPU job completed before the Cancel button received a real pointer click; the test was racing after completion rather than proving in-flight cancellation.

**Implementation**
- `public/creator-local-capture.js`: impose a four-second preview-start deadline. A pending/rejected `video.play()` cannot leave the camera stream active indefinitely; the existing fail-closed abort releases tracks and exposes the explicit unsupported-browser fallback. Keep the separate one-minute capture limit.
- `browser-tests/public-experience.spec.js`: add a regression case for a never-settling play Promise; verify no preview/download and track release; exercise the scheduled 60-second stop callback without freezing browser media startup with a fake clock; hold local-compute permission verification pending until a real Cancel click and assert the original pixels survive. No browser is skipped and no assertion is weakened.
- Synthetic execution of the **actual patched client script** with virtual timers and mocked DOM/media: a pending play request hit its 4000-ms deadline, released its track and showed the fallback; a successful request retained preview and the separate 60-second budget. This is not a complete Playwright run.
- Primary reference: MDN `HTMLMediaElement.play()` notes that start may remain delayed pending user permission, so applications must handle non-immediate playback outcomes.

**Remaining generated-file release gate:** exact-head CI now identifies only one stale generator delta in `data/capability-inventory.json`: remove absent `.github/workflows/codex-pr508-regenerate-capability-once.yml` and change `infrastructureSourceFileCount` 49→48. This two-line diff was validated against current repository content, but connector attempts to upload/create the resulting ~21 MB Git blob both failed with a transport-level h2 error. **The generated inventory is still unchanged and CI remains blocked.** Regenerate with `node scripts/generate-capability-inventory.cjs --write` on the exact branch in a writable checkout, inspect the two-line diff and commit the artifact. Do not bypass `--check` or add a fake workflow to satisfy stale metadata.

Do not merge or deploy until all required exact-head checks pass and the GitHub governance/release controls are confirmed.

records.title: feat(reliability): signed recovery sensors, durable anti-replay and fenced retry controls
records.head: feature/autonomic-diagnostics-2026-10-08
records.source_body:
# SONARA autonomic recovery — Phases 1–7 (draft, no activation)

**SAFETY:** This PR is review-only. No merge, live database migration, live sensor endpoint, secret provisioning, cron/worker activation, live provider call or production deployment is authorized by this change.

## Existing recovery foundation (Phases 1–6)
- Deterministic allowlisted runtime recovery planning, optional-provider retry delay and deadlines, cooldowns, tenant/idempotency checks and SLO evidence.
- Private PostgreSQL repair and durable delayed retry ledgers; atomic due claims, claim fencing, immutable audit, service_role RPCs and no blind replay of ambiguous external outcomes.
- Server-only worker that checks current authorization, provider idempotency, operation fencing, fresh deadlines and explicit operator pause before a single provider effect; independent post-action verification.
- Read-only stalled and ambiguous retry reconciliation. Native PostgreSQL replay includes role/tenant/fencing tests and a two-connection delayed retry claim race.

## Phase 7 completed source changes
- `lib/sonara-signed-recovery-observation.cjs`: custom SONARA-owned HMAC-SHA256 raw-body protocol, constant-time verification, strict <=4 KiB payload shape, signed timestamp window, per-sensor secret requirement, canonical lowercase nonce, fail-closed replay-claim contract.
- `lib/sonara-postgres-sensor-nonces.cjs`: server-only injected service_role RPC adapter; admits only a database-confirmed true.
- `supabase/migrations/20261008214500_autonomic_signed_sensor_nonces.sql`: private `sonara_private.autonomic_sensor_nonces` with RLS; atomic unique (sensor_id,nonce); strict timestamp and TTL policy; public-schema RPC revoked from all browser roles, granted only to service_role. This is **unapplied**.
- `lib/sonara-signed-recovery-ingress.cjs`: composes original signed bytes → trusted registry → private nonce claim → existing bounded durable retry scheduler. No HTTP route or provider handler and disabled by default.
- `tests/sonara-signed-recovery-observation.test.js` (10 cases) and `tests/sonara-signed-recovery-ingress.test.js` (6 cases): cryptographic HMAC, replay, forged body, cross-tenant, revoked/absent secret, disabled path and persistence-response failures.
- `tests/sql/autonomic-sensor-nonce-role-matrix.sql`: native disposable PostgreSQL roles, timestamp windows, duplicate and per-sensor namespace proof.
- `scripts/verify-migration-replay.mjs`: requires native role-matrix proof **and two concurrent PostgreSQL sessions** where exactly one can claim a shared signed nonce; asserts one committed row.
- `supabase/applied-migration-checksums.json`: signed sensor migration SHA-256 `da1feffd17da0bf31a4aec517920f53cd1546a5260019115cfd98d3f058bd66e`.
- `docs/engineering/AUTONOMIC_RECOVERY_PHASE_7_2026_10_08.md`: explicit protocol, limitations, risks and gate.

## Evidence / blockers
- Targeted code-syntax checks passed for five Phase 7 JS CommonJS source/test files; native-replay snippet syntax passed. **This is not functional test execution.**
- Phase 7 Mocha tests and PostgreSQL replay are committed, but **not yet proven passing** on the exact commit; GitHub Actions were queued/pending on last inspection.
- GitHub administration branch protection state remains unverified. No real per-sensor vault integration, key rotation, rate-limited HTTPS ingress, bounded nonce purging, or authorized tenant/provider canary exists yet.
- Caution: protocol here is **SONARA-only**; don't use it to validate Stripe, GitHub or other third-party webhook signatures.

## Required release gate
Exact-commit full green CI/build/lint/typecheck/security → native PostgreSQL 16/17/18 role, migration and two-session race proofs → tenant isolation/real signature and operation authorization → review immutable checksum + target Supabase project → operator-approved staging → verified provider idempotency and kill switch → explicit approval for single-tenant canary. Keep production disabled until all gates pass.

Sources: OWASP Webhook Security https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Webhook_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html; PostgreSQL SELECT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-select.html.

## Phase 9 — SLO window confidence and product isolation

- Conservative 5m/1h and 30m/6h SLO burn evaluator now demands long-window history and coverage across multiple time buckets to avoid treating short telemetry bursts as sustained long-window evidence.
- New read-only per-product SLO isolation for SONARA One, Business Builder, Creator Studio and Growth Studio, using closed product labels and no raw route/tenant identifiers.
- Eight local isolated SLO regression tests and six per-suite isolation cases passed. These are **not equivalent to native GitHub CI or PostgreSQL replay**.
- New documentation: `docs/engineering/AUTONOMIC_RECOVERY_PHASE_9_2026_10_08.md`.
- No production activation; all existing exact-head approval, migration, tenant security and canary gates remain blocking.


## Phase 10 — Verifiable offline per-suite SLO evidence

- Added `lib/sonara-offline-slo-evidence.cjs`, a fixed-cardinality JSONL event accumulator that checks the existing server HTTP event shape, recomputed product/journey labels, HTTP outcomes and timestamps, duplicate request IDs, unknown routes and bounded data capacity.
- Added `scripts/diagnose-suite-slo-evidence.mjs` for optional reproducible offline reports (`--input`, optional `--as-of`). It never pages, performs provider actions or consumes live credentials; files are explicitly not authenticated collector output.
- Added eight pure accumulator tests and four subprocess integration tests, plus `docs/engineering/AUTONOMIC_RECOVERY_PHASE_10_2026_10_08.md`.
- Isolated core checks: **7/7 + 8/8**; separate CLI grammar/exit code smoke passed with a stubbed accumulator. **Full Mocha integration tests, exact-head GitHub workflows and PostgreSQL replay remain unverified** until CI concludes.
- This PR remains draft. No merge, applied database migration, autonomous activation or production deployment was performed.


## October 9 release-gate repair evidence
- Historical exact-head CI exposed **real failures**, not merely queued jobs: native PostgreSQL replay failed at the obsolete P1 25-policy definition fixture; the Mocha suite reported an orphan-table scanner misreading `sonara_private` as a table, plus a stale handoff count.
- Repaired schema-qualified table parsing, documented private recovery table dispositions, added sandbox regression for private tables, and changed the rolled-back P1 probe to check 25 **post-20261008100000 hardened definitions** rather than obsolete pre-migration expressions. This retains fail-closed role, predicate, and duplicate-policy checks.
- Independent full-tree measurement: PR #510 **534 Mocha files / 166 migrations**; dependent PR #551 **535 Mocha files / 167 migrations**. The bounded handoff documents were reconciled to those counts.
- Changes remain test-only / code-review-only: no live migrations, no worker enablement, no repairs, and no merge to main. **Fresh exact-head CI and native PostgreSQL replay are required before claiming these fixes pass.**
- Parent and stacked branches were reconciled with a recorded two-parent merge commit; PR #551 remains draft and requires PR #510 first.


## October 9 — exact-head CI failure triage and corrections
Latest completed failing logs (prior head) were inspected, not inferred from queued status:
- **Native replay:** P1 hardened 25-policy check advanced; the subscriptions test failed because it demanded two duplicate policies and a single historical deparse. The rollback fixture now requires 1–2 *authenticated, owner-scoped SELECT* policies with a known safe predicate; it only dry-run-drops a duplicate when **both** have been validated. Unknown/missing/unsafe policies still fail closed. No historical migration or production RLS changed.
- **Node/SONARA tests:** **7,205 passing, 1 failing**. The failing `orphan-tables` assertion used `sonara-migration-columns.cjs`, which recognized only public/unqualified tables. It now parses qualified `sonara_private` table definitions, and regression coverage requires all five private recovery tables to have real parsed columns. Exact-head source regex was exercised against the five committed migration definitions (5/5).
- **Browser Quality:** WebKit had 24 failures in the previous run; Chromium and Firefox jobs succeeded. WebKit remains a separate unresolved gate and was not concealed or relaxed.
- Both draft branches have been reconciled. **No merge, deployment, production migration, runtime activation or real provider effect**. Current exact-head workflow results remain queued/pending; *do not claim full green*.
Source interpretation checked against PostgreSQL `pg_policies` documentation: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/view-pg-policies.html .

records.title: fix(worker): require unique, scoped evidence before canary activation
records.head: fix/event-consumer-canary-evidence-20261008
records.source_body:
## Scope: one-tenant event consumer with positive proof, safe retry contracts and no production activation

### Reproduced source defects
- Canary could falsely pass 20 duplicate "delivered" rows, 20 null handler durations counted as 0ms, or 20 second-attempt deliveries.
- A privileged claim was trusted without validating returned organization, kind and producer.
- Any handler outcome other than explicit `{ok:false}` was incorrectly reported `delivered`.
- Synchronous or rejected queue claim/settle adapter calls escaped without scoped structured failure reporting.
- **Latest:** synthetic handler timeout settled `retry` while the timed-out handler's promise continued; a later attempt could repeat external side effects.

### Changes
- Require unique expected fresh outbox IDs, valid samples and all-first-attempt delivery before canary activation.
- Scope-check claimed tenant/kind/producer before invoking a handler.
- Only `{ok:true}` indicates handler completion; malformed output and unclassified failures are quarantined.
- Classify thrown queue adapter faults as structured `claim_failed` / `settlement_failed`, no secret-bearing exception text in telemetry.
- Handler timeout `handler_timeout` now settles `dead_lettered` instead of automatically replaying; the original provider operation may still finish, so reconciliation is mandatory.
- Automatic retry permitted only for **explicit `retryable:true`** outcomes. Preserve existing exponential backoff/attempt cap for safe retries.
- Enforce `handlerTimeoutMs` positive safe integer and strictly below 5-minute claim lease minus 10-second settlement reserve.
- Add **13 defensive test cases** in the existing `tests/event-consumer-readiness.test.js` (no test file count change). Research and measured evidence in `docs/research/2026-10-08-reddit-event-worker-reliability-hardening.md`.

### Verification and limitations
- Earlier baseline false-success classes reproduced from main; latest timeout baseline returned `retry` while handler remained in flight.
- **23/23 runnable registered test bodies passed** against latest branch code in a V8 isolated harness with injected mocks. One canonical application runtime gate test was excluded. This is **not** complete Node/Mocha, GitHub CI or staging RLS/DB/provider proof.
- Must run exact-head pnpm install, Node 24 Mocha, full CI and native PostgreSQL replay; verify two-tenant test, queue lease expiry/fencing, real canary and provider receipts in an authorized staging project.

### Release conditions
Draft only. Do not merge, activate workers, send customer messages, process live money, enable social autopost, or deploy/reactivate production without fully passing checks, human review, approvals and verified rollback. Separate from PR #508 CI, #509 activation analytics and #512 PostgREST response integrity.

## Reproduced defects
- A successful enqueue API response could report another tenant's row as newly created.
- A malformed successful filtered-claim response could be silently treated as idle.

- Validate response array shape, single-row cardinality, tenant/idempotency identity on new and deduplicated events, claimed state, **exact worker claim-owner fencing token**, filtered kind/producer, and settled row ID/tenant/final state.
- Distinguish genuine empty claim/settlement arrays from unreadable PostgREST evidence.
- Extend the existing `tests/event-outbox.test.js` with claim-owner mismatch/null/empty cases for both filtered/unfiltered RPCs, preserving the Mocha file count. Existing earlier receipt-integrity regressions remain.
- Research documentation: `docs/research/2026-10-08-reddit-postgrest-outbox-response-integrity.md`.

## Verification
- Reproduced 3 false-success classes against original main source with injected PostgREST responses.
- Before/after source probe: a stale claim-owner token was accepted by both claim methods at the earlier PR head, but rejected by both in this revision with `claim_identity_mismatch`.
- **28/28 runnable repository test bodies** passed in an isolated JS harness against this latest branch. Three additional tests require full Node runtime and were excluded. **This is not a full Node/Mocha or Postgres integration test.**
- Required: `pnpm exec mocha tests/event-outbox.test.js tests/event-consumer-readiness.test.js`, full exact-head CI, RLS/role/SQL staging tests and same-idempotency-key replay proof.

records.title: fix(mobile): separate US Play external content links from alternative billing
records.head: codex/distinguish-google-us-external-links-20261008
records.source_body:
## Independent 2026 policy finding
Google Play distinguishes two separate United States programs: **in-app alternative billing** and **external content links**. They require different Play Console enrollments, APIs, disclosures and reporting. The external-content-links guidance specifies an **October 1, 2026** transaction reporting / fee start and a separately extended **December 1, 2026** deadline for successful external-app-download reporting and fees; the app-download deadline does not defer purchase reporting.

Official policies:
- https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16497028
- https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16470497

## Implemented
- Add distinct pure method `google_us_external_link` to `lib/sonara-mobile-billing-classification.cjs`, separate from `google_us_alternative` and `google_play_billing`.
- Require reviewed external-links enrollment, APIs, destination, prelink disclosure, transaction reporting, service-fee acceptance and customer support/refunds. Refuse unapproved region/missing proof; prevent cross-program evidence reuse.
- Return only a safe **external_link_only** advisory candidate; **no checkout, entitlement, navigation, store purchase or app-download capability is activated**.
- Add adversarial tests and corrected date/program documentation.

## Validation
The pure module compiles and 13 targeted smoke assertions passed, including 7 independently missing evidence fields, non-US, cross-program and wrong-platform denials. Full Mocha and exact-head CI are **not yet verified**. Test with `pnpm exec mocha tests/mobile-store-billing-classification.test.js`, `pnpm run verify:launch`, and the complete native replay/browser/security matrix before any merge. Avoid merging while P0 CI in PR #508 remains red.

## Non-actions
No live Stripe payments, no native billing APIs, no app-store actions, no production deployment, no Supabase writes. Current site-offline release instruction preserved.

records.title: fix(media): fail closed on unplayable camera previews across browsers
records.head: fix/camera-preview-webkit-validated-20261008
records.source_body:
## Stacked P0/P2 browser/media reliability fix

Depends on draft #508; this branch contains #508's exact source commit and is temporarily targeted at `main` to run the required main-targeted browser-quality CI. The combined diff MUST NOT be merged ahead of #508's approval; once #508 lands, reconcile/rebase and review the narrowed patch.

### Root cause and production fix
- CI WebKit reports `canvas.captureStream()` but is not guaranteed to yield a playable, dimensioned camera preview. The previous code awaited `video.play()` indefinitely, kept permissioned media tracks live and left "Take photo" hidden.
- Camera startup now rejects empty video-track streams and requires a completed playback with nonzero dimensions before exposing the photo action. A 4s deadline fails closed: all tracks, timers and preview state are released; original local-file workflows remain available.
- Browser/OS permission denials retain their explicit status.

### Test/CI improvements
- Browser fixtures check the actual product outcome (ready preview vs visible denial), not API existence.
- Delayed OS prompts use deterministic fake stop-capable tracks so the revocation and late-arrival tests do not depend on browser-specific canvas capture semantics; no test is skipped.
- The mock-clock timeout test advances the preview-start deadline explicitly.
- Each Chromium/Firefox/WebKit lane still runs all browser contracts independently, with `--workers=1` to avoid local server contention.

### Verification
Source syntax compiled with JS parser for both changed JS files. Exact-head Playwright/WebKit/Firefox/Chromium, full SONARA CI, and browser artifact review remain required. Do not merge #508 or this stacked PR until all mandatory gates pass. The current P0 capability inventory generation failure remains separately unresolved and is not masked.

### External references
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/play
- https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions
- https://playwright.dev/docs/test-webserver

No production migration/deploy, payments, customer data, camera permission, provider activation or mobile store release.

records.title: fix(release): attest every required exact-SHA CI job before production access
records.head: fix/release-required-job-attestation-20261008
records.source_body:
## P0 safety gap
A green GitHub Actions workflow can contain skipped, neutral, incomplete, or missing jobs. SONARA's existing controlled production deployment already checks exact-main SHA and six workflow-level conclusions, but it did not independently validate the mandatory job matrix, including all nine PostgreSQL replay cells and Node 24/26.

## Implementation
- `scripts/verify-exact-sha-release-jobs.cjs`: read-only GitHub job-level attestation, require all six workflow names on current protected main SHA and exact `push` event. Independently check job `run_id`, completion, `success`, unique mandatory identities, and complete paginated response. Only the manual/nonblocking Node 27 lane may be skipped.
- `tests/exact-sha-job-attestation.test.js`: regression for skipped native SQL replay, missing and duplicated Node checks, stale or unprotected main, truncated job API, wrong run IDs, GitHub failure, and pre-credential workflow order.
- `.github/workflows/controlled-production-deploy.yml`: invoke the gate after existing exact-SHA run gate and before production governance, dependency installation, provider credentials, or DB changes.

## Safety and required verification
No production secret is read or emitted by this script; it uses GitHub Actions read-only job endpoints. No database schema migration or deployment is made. Locally evaluated the module on a complete fake matrix (pass) and with one skipped PostgreSQL replay job (blocked); **this is not full CI proof**. Keep the PR draft until its exact-head Node compatibility/full suite checks pass.

## External blockers
Production release still requires GitHub admin to protect `main` and enforce PR status checks and independent environment reviewers (issue #460); live status was unprotected. Restore production website only under a separately approved controlled release. Do not auto-merge or publish this PR while any CI is red.

### Hardened after initial draft
- Mandatory conditional **step** attestation added. A green Docker job with absent Dockerfile no longer qualifies: both build and image smoke must execute successfully. Native replay must run its real PostgreSQL step in all 9 lanes; Node 24/26 must actually execute Test and Build, and main application job must run full tests and DB verification.
- Synthetic probe: complete 18-job matrix passed; same evidence with a skipped Docker build step was refused. This is partial synthetic verification, not production approval.
- `docs/HANDOFF_PROMPT.md` synchronized against `.mocharc.json`: 517 matched Mocha files on this head.
- Owner/operator documentation with exact job context names, API failure policy and path-filtered browser caveat: `docs/release/EXACT_SHA_JOB_ATTESTATION_2026-10-08.md`.
- Live post-migration read-only tenant checks in active Supabase preview: both existing A/B members can see own org/membership only, not the other's. Neither these read checks nor the new gate authorize customer writes or release.

records.title: Revoke browser grants from reviewed server-only tables
records.head: hardening/browser-role-grants-20261008
records.source_body:
## Purpose

This is deliberately stacked on PR #513 rather than main. Current main is red after the 18-PR integration merge, so database hardening must not bypass exact-head recovery.

Live Supabase review found 66 RLS-enabled public tables with no policy. That finding is not automatically a vulnerability: many are intentionally server-only. The actionable second-layer gap is narrower.

Exactly 13 reviewed server-only tables still expose broad table DML privileges to both `anon` and `authenticated`, even though RLS/no-policy currently denies rows. This migration removes that unnecessary dependency on RLS always remaining correctly enabled.

## Migration

Adds `20261008110000_revoke_browser_grants_server_only_tables.sql`.

Targets only:
- audit_logs
- billing_events
- db_health_snapshots
- platform_jobs
- prompt_templates
- sonara_control_plane_checks
- sonara_launch_settings
- sonara_realtime_channel_registry
- sonara_storage_bucket_registry
- sonara_ui_capability_registry
- sonara_webhook_verification_registry
- sonara_worker_job_registry
- sonara_write_api_registry

The migration:
- requires every target to exist, have RLS enabled and have zero policies;
- permits only two browser-DML preflight states: all four DML grants (the live drift being repaired) or none (a clean fresh replay already hardened by default privileges);
- aborts on partial grant drift;
- revokes all table privileges from `anon` and `authenticated`;
- proves every browser table privilege is gone afterwards;
- proves `service_role` retains SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE;
- creates no policies, drops no tables and mutates no customer rows.

## Evidence integration

- existing privilege-hardening tests extended; no new Mocha test file added;
- migration checksum pinned;
- generated migration counts advanced 163 → 164;
- replay-safe precondition prevents production drift from breaking clean database replay.

## Merge/deploy boundary

Do **not** retarget or merge this into main until PR #513 is green and accepted.
Do **not** apply this migration to Supabase until its eventual exact-head main commit is green.
This PR performs no live database change.

records.head: fix/release-attestation-source-branch-20261008
records.source_body:
## P0 exact-SHA release attestation hardening — stacked on #516

GitHub's REST API provides `head_branch` on both workflow-run and workflow-job records, and `head_sha` on job records. Prior attestation selected successful push runs by workflow name/SHA but did not require the run's source branch to be `main`; it also did not confirm the job's own source ref and SHA. Another pushed branch pointing at the same SHA could therefore provide apparently valid evidence.

### Implementation
- Only accept required `push` workflow runs if `head_branch === "main"` **and** `head_sha` equals the protected current main commit; enforce this in both selection paths.
- Require every returned job to attest both `head_branch === "main"` and `head_sha === exactSha`, in addition to matching run ID and successful steps.
- Strengthen synthetic fixtures and add adversarial regression cases for other-branch push runs, same-SHA wrong-branch jobs, wrong-commit jobs, and correct selection when a newer branch run exists.

### Independent references
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs
- https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets

### Safety and proof boundaries
This is code-only, **draft** and depends on #516. Its temporary target is `main` solely to trigger required CI on the integrated candidate; review must separate #516's underlying changes and must not merge this combined branch until #516 is independently approved and reconciled. It does not write to any production account, apply migrations, deploy, merge, or change live environment settings. Required before merge: `pnpm exec mocha tests/exact-sha-job-attestation.test.js`, exact-head full Node/CI/security/SQL/browser gates, and human review. The local sandbox does not have network access to clone and run the repository; these source changes have not yet received Mocha/CI proof. This attestation complements but does not replace real branch protection, required reviews and a deliberate red-merge-denial test.

### Follow-up: canonical workflow source identity
GitHub workflow display names are not unique. In addition to head SHA/branch checks, both run-selection code paths now require the canonical `.github/workflows/*.yml` path for each of the six mandatory release workflows. Two adversarial tests reject successful same-name lookalike workflows and ignore an unrelated-branch newer run. Canonical paths were verified against the actual repository workflow directory. No checks were downgraded.

Current exact PR head: `828192498ef87df2f53ecfc1631bd40bd7e2d95a`. CI is required; synthetic tests are committed but no exact-head green result is claimed.

## Release safety gap
The controlled production deployment currently requires six successful exact-SHA **push** workflows but does not require successful Chromium/Firefox/WebKit browser acceptance. PR #508 exposed genuine WebKit camera and Firefox navigation failures, even while native migration replay was green.

records.title: security(release): restrict production secrets to consuming GitHub Actions steps
records.head: fix/release-secrets-step-isolation-20261008
records.source_body:
## P0: reduce production secret scope in the controlled release workflow

**Root cause:** The controlled production workflow declared `VERCEL_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID`, and `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` at `jobs.validate-migrate-deploy.env`. Every step, including third-party dependency installation, compilation, tests and security scans, inherits these credentials after environment approval, although those steps do not require production access.

### Code changes
- Keep only non-sensitive Vercel project routing identifiers and public health URLs in job-level environment.
- Inject each protected secret explicitly through step-level `env:` on **only** the protected credential preflight and actual consuming steps. Eight consuming/preflight steps receive least-privilege assignments; build/test/lint/scan do not.
- Preserve protected production environment, exact-SHA and required-job evidence gates, credential preflight, provider checks, rollback, migrations and approval order. Do not emit credentials in logs, artifact files or GITHUB_ENV.
- Add two regression tests to the existing `tests/exact-sha-job-attestation.test.js` (no new Mocha file): job-level environment has zero `secrets.*`, every credential has an exact reviewed allowlist of receiving steps, and release checks precede credential access.

### Evidence
- Repository source inspection identified job-level secrets and actual step consumers.
- Read-back of committed workflow verified **zero job-level secrets**, 34 preserved named steps, and the intended exact per-secret step scopes. JavaScript test source parses successfully.
- **Additional isolated execution:** 11/11 existing and newly added test callbacks passed when the committed CJS verifier and committed tests were executed in an isolated V8 harness against the committed workflow source, with mocked file reads and GitHub API. This does **not** exercise native Node/Mocha, real GitHub Actions runner YAML parsing, CI or production secrets. Full exact-head checks must still pass and the workflow must be independently reviewed before merge.

### Dependency and rollout boundary
This branch includes draft #516's release-job attestation improvements. Its PR targets `main` so the complete candidate receives required CI; do not merge ahead of independent review and reconciliation of #516 or ignore any red status. No deployment, migration, provider credential retrieval, Stripe action, production website reactivation, or customer data mutation took place.

### Research
- GitHub step-scoped secret injection: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets
- GitHub workflow syntax and env inheritance: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax
- Required GitHub environment reviewer protections: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments

Owner still needs branch/ruleset enforcement and independent production-environment approvals, issue #460.

### Adversarial regression proof
The isolated 11-case harness passed on the candidate workflow. Three injected regressions were then evaluated: (1) reintroducing a job-level Vercel token failed the job-secret test, (2) adding that token to dependency installation failed the step allowlist test, and (3) removing Supabase access token from the migration dry-run step failed the consumer completeness test. This demonstrates the two new assertions detect both exposure and missing credentials. It remains a synthetic harness, **not hosted CI or full Mocha**.

## Unified release attestation — draft, NOT production approved

Consolidates the exact-SHA job identity safeguards of **#516 and #518** with the manual cross-browser release proof from **#521**. This is an integration branch forked at #518's reviewed head, with #521's workflow and regression test applied.

### Additional hardening implemented here
- Require every `Browser Quality` child job on the *same main SHA*: `Playwright chromium`, `Playwright firefox`, `Playwright webkit`.
- Require successful browser contract and evidence-upload steps; never accept skipped, neutral, absent or duplicated jobs.
- Accept only the latest manually dispatched `Browser Quality` workflow on protected `main`. All six original required release workflows remain strict `push` evidence.
- Query GitHub run listing by `head_sha` and `branch=main` without incorrectly filtering out `workflow_dispatch`.
- Add adversarial tests for the false-green conditions and regenerate the Mocha count to 518.

### Blocking conditions
**Do not merge** without exact-head CI, independent approval and GitHub branch protection. Current `main` was observed unprotected; this source PR cannot change that setting.

**Do not deploy, publish mobile apps, run production migrations or handle live payments** on this branch. Re-run the post-merge official release gate against protected main separately. Preserve #516, #518, #521 for traceability until the integration diff and test evidence are verified.

Database conflict: #517 and #520 both introduce version `20261008110000`, so they must never both enter the applied migration history without a canonical resolution. #522 is stacked on #520.

See `docs/release/UNIFIED_EXACT_SHA_BROWSER_JOB_GATE_2026-10-08.md` for documentation and official GitHub references.

### Credential boundary added during consolidation
The release gate now runs `release-attestation-preflight` **without any production environment or provider secrets**. The protected `validate-migrate-deploy` job has an explicit `needs: release-attestation-preflight` dependency and cannot run if this independent read-only attestation fails. Dedicated adversarial tests assert the preflight job contains no production secrets and that the protected deployment job retains them.

### Additional least-privilege hardening and CI contract repair (2026-10-08)
- Consolidates #523's production-token scoping into this already unified branch to avoid merging overlapping workflow changes independently. The four job-wide Vercel/Supabase credentials were removed. Eighteen precise bindings remain across eight named consuming/preflight steps; no production token is available in the preflight or inherited by install/build/test/lint steps.
- Corrects `scripts/verify-agent-development-sync.mjs` to isolate the **named production job** rather than the first `env` / `steps` pair (which began failing after the new credential-free preflight). This was a real CI failure in run `37831069182`, not an optional test to bypass.
- Adds two exact credential allowlist regression tests in the existing release test file; no new Mocha file. Five deliberately injected negative contract cases were rejected by an isolated static harness, but the complete hosted test matrix is **not yet green**.
- Documents residual same-runner risk and recommends a separate unprivileged build job with attested immutable artifact as subsequent security work.

### Outstanding review and production blockers
- Required release evidence on final main SHA, real branch protection and production reviewers, native PostgreSQL 16–18 replay and full three-browser acceptance remain mandatory.
- CI on antecedent PR #525 head `f8d5618` had six failing workflows, including a reproducible agent-sync fixture assumption (addressed in this branch); the present head has not yet been shown all-green.
- Related security patch #523 and attestation PRs #516/#518/#521 must be reconciled as **one reviewed release change**, not silently merged one after another.
- Keep production OFFLINE: no merge, provider execution, live migrations or release approval from this PR.

GitHub `main` protection and protected-environment settings still require administrator configuration; source code does not supply that governance. CI on the exact PR head remains authoritative.

records.title: recovery: stop treating schema checkpoints as customer-data backups
records.head: hardening/recovery-evidence-truth-20261008
records.source_body:
## Why

The controlled production workflow records a UTC timestamp and a schema-only dump before migrations. The current connected Supabase organization is on the Free plan, where SONARA has no proven PITR path.

Despite that, the workflow summary and rollback runbook still called the timestamp a **PITR restore target**. That is false operational evidence: a timestamp does not become a recoverable point merely because it was recorded.

## Change

- rename the job-summary value to **Pre-migration incident timestamp (UTC)**;
- explicitly record `Data-backup status: not_proven_by_this_artifact`;
- update the rollback runbook so destructive rollback stops unless an actual recovery mechanism was established and restore-tested first;
- state plainly that a hand-written down-migration can reverse schema changes but cannot recover lost/corrupt customer data;
- update `MONITORING_AND_BACKUPS.md` so schema evidence and customer-data recovery are not conflated;
- extend the existing rollback-summary regression test so the false PITR wording cannot return.

## Recovery boundary

A 10/10 recovery posture still requires one of:

1. eligible managed backups/PITR plus a dated successful restore drill; or
2. encrypted approved off-site logical database backup plus separate Supabase Storage-object backup, with both restored into an isolated environment and reconciled.

GitHub artifacts remain schema/evidence only and must not hold customer data.

## Stack order

This is intentionally stacked after the database/release hardening chain:

`#508 → #520 → #522 → #524 → this PR`.

No production backup, restore, migration, or deployment is performed here.

## Summary — bounded live calculation forms on existing authenticated SONARA research page

This draft PR consolidates deterministic game/scientific modules with a functional read-only website workbench. It is **not merged, not production-deployed, not a real-money gaming service, and not a brokerage**.

### Source implementation
- Existing source-level kernels: probability and roulette theoretical EV, card combinatorics/poker hand types, zero-sum game theory, tic-tac-toe minimax, synthetic moving-average backtests, coordinate geometry, trigonometry, calculus, fixed-timestep educational physics, film timing, MIDI notes, chords, and narrative tension metadata.
- `lib/sonara-simulation-integration.cjs`: 15 allowlisted cross-studio research operations; no network, DB, auth or payment side effects; no studio privilege escalation.
- **New** `lib/sonara-research-workbench.cjs`: three genuinely executable low-cost GET study forms for rectangular area (Business Builder), MIDI chords (Creator Studio), 2×2 payoff equilibria (Growth Studio). Forms submit only to the existing customer-guarded `/market-intelligence/invention-systems` route; no independent execution endpoint, user-data storage or mutation.
- Existing route `routes/invention-systems-routes.cjs` now displays the forms and the earlier fixed-input examples. It reuses injected `requireCustomer`. The response sets `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` to reduce study-input leakage.
- Dedicated bounds: allowlisted study/fields, strict numeric parsing, decimal ranges, input key and byte caps, immutable form definitions and escaped text. Accessible native labels, select and submit controls, error text and output element.
- Update to `docs/architecture/SONARA_CROSS_STUDIO_SIMULATION_INTEGRATION_2026-10-08.md` documents release/security/performance/worker and rights gates.

### Tests run
- **118/118** focused cases passed in an **isolated JavaScript V8 test harness**, executing the current GitHub module/test source, with Node assertions and Express route interactions simulated. All nine test suites checked; 0 failures.
- **Not yet verified:** pinned Node/pnpm full Mocha run, lint, audit, build, typecheck, route/browser accessibility, tenant and authentication integration, production exact-head CI and release infrastructure. Any queued checks remain unresolved.

### Product authority restrictions
- Research calculations only; no account creation, saved scenarios, casino RNG, wagering, payments, redeemable credit, broker/order execution, custody, financial advice or customer campaigns.
- Higher-cost simulation, Monte Carlo, gaming search, physics and paper-trading engines are **NOT** exposed through user-submitted forms. Their source stays internal research until independent server-auth, per-tenant rate quotas, cost metering, observability and worker isolation are proved.
- GET values appear in URL; page warns not to enter private information. No third-party script or media dependency is added.
- No SQL migration, provider credential, Stripe, Supabase RLS, native mobile or production deployment has been changed.

### Required pre-merge gates
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm audit --audit-level moderate`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm run build`, exact-SHA GitHub CI, production release/migration/security evidence, accessibility/browser tests and authorized promotion to production. Do **not** merge while mandatory checks are red/unknown.

records.title: security(platform): validate durable rate decisions and close unmetered scope gaps
records.head: fix/shared-rate-limit-rpc-boundary-20261008
records.source_body:
## Cross-suite reliability and abuse-control hardening (draft)

**Scope:** One existing shared `lib/sonara-rate-limit.cjs` enforcement boundary used by authentication, public booking/leads, marketplace/merchant writes and Creator/Growth submit paths. No changes to rate limits, subscription entitlements, billing records, user roles, or production data.

### Reproduced defects
1. The SQL function `public.sonara_consume_rate_limit` declares `RETURNS TABLE (allowed boolean, remaining integer, retry_after_seconds integer)` and emits exactly one row. The HTTP caller previously accepted the first element of *any* array, or a bare object, without checking cardinality. It also coerced negative, missing, and string counters via `Number(value)||0` and trusted a positive `allowed` flag with inconsistent counters.
2. Without an RPC deadline, a durable counter could delay any protected request indefinitely until infrastructure timeout.
3. `scopes:["subject"]` with an absent subject produced zero buckets and therefore no protection. Empty, duplicate, or mistyped scope configurations could likewise yield no counted budget.

### Changes
- Require **one and only one** structured PostgREST decision; validate allowed boolean, safe integer counters, remaining in `[0,maxAttempts]`, allowed retry=0, and denied retry>=1 with remaining=0.
- Fail invalid or missing durable evidence into the already-established **bounded, explicitly degraded per-instance fallback**, never mark a malformed decision `durable:true`.
- Set a 4-second abort deadline on the rate-limit RPC; fallback remains observable via `rate_limit.degraded`. **Important:** per-instance fallback is weaker than multi-instance protection and is not a production-grade substitute for the database; follow-up circuit-breaker, multi-tenant load and chaos tests remain necessary.
- Refuse empty, duplicate or unrecognized limiter scopes at factory construction.
- For subject-only limiters without a usable subject, meter the request against a hashed IP budget instead of admitting it without counting.

### Regression evidence
- Six regression cases added to existing `tests/auth-rate-limit.test.js`, so no new Mocha test file or handoff count change.
- Isolated V8 execution of the checked-in module: **6/6 security-focused scenarios passed**, with mocked PostgREST and crypto module loading (NOT full Node/Mocha).
- Before/after repro: original code returned `{allowed:true,durable:true,remaining:-3,retryAfterSeconds:-1}` for a malformed RPC response; patched code returned `degraded:true,durable:false` and enforced a finite in-memory budget.
- JavaScript parser compiled both changed source files.

### Security/proxy context
- Vercel states it overwrites incoming `X-Forwarded-For` to prevent IP spoofing on its platform: https://vercel.com/docs/headers/request-headers. Do not assume this property holds behind another proxy or a directly exposed self-hosted runtime. MDN advises trusting only headers inserted by an explicitly trusted proxy: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Forwarded-For
- PostgREST response shapes: https://postgrest.org/en/stable/references/api/functions.html

### Required before merge/release
Run targeted `pnpm exec mocha tests/auth-rate-limit.test.js tests/a-rate-limiter-that-fails-open-says-so.test.js`, Node 22/24/26 compatibility, exact-head full CI, tenant/RLS/native replay, browser, supply-chain and load/saturation tests. Reconcile with current P0 release/security PRs and protect main under issue #460. No production deployment, customer data, migration, credentials, payment or website activation. Preserve the intentionally offline website.

records.title: fix(growth): reconcile uncertain Resend batches instead of replaying messages
records.head: fix/growth-dispatch-ambiguous-delivery-20261008
records.source_body:
## Critical correctness issue and proof

The old Growth dispatcher treated a malformed/short Resend batch response as a reason to replay those exact recipients individually. A response can be lost after the provider has accepted the email, so the old fallback could double-send messages. A second false-success path counted individual HTTP 200 responses as accepted without parsing a provider message ID. Both were reproduced from actual source patterns.

Resend officially documents an ID in successful individual responses, one ID per batch recipient, and 24-hour request idempotency retention. See `docs/research/2026-10-08-growth-idempotency-and-uncertain-delivery.md`.

## Changes (9 files; no migrations/dependency additions)

- Derive operation-scoped SHA-256 Resend idempotency keys for individual and batch POSTs from tenant, campaign, send attempt, scope and full request body. The header contains no raw email addresses or secrets.
- Only complete nonempty, distinct batch IDs or a nonempty individual response ID count as verified acceptance.
- HTTP 2xx without a valid receipt, transport failure and indeterminate provider responses are `delivery_unconfirmed`, never automatically replayed, not billed as confirmed usage and are stored for reconciliation.
- Stop subsequent sends after an uncertain batch; retain known-not-attempted recipients independently. A successful read from the historical append-only table cannot turn unknown recipient state into a safe-to-resend remainder.
- Use `growth_campaign_sends.reason='provider_outcome_unknown'` with its existing `status='failed'` storage-envelope vocabulary, while the public API returns a distinct `uncertain` list. Do not present those as verified failures.
- Return and audit unconfirmed counts. Do not tell owners to use the remainder action while unresolved provider results exist.
- Retarget older unit/route tests that formerly required the unsafe fallback or pretended an empty individual HTTP 200 was success; verify no later calls, confirmed-only billing, and consent-scoped delivery.
- Revise operations plan and research. Do not rewrite the historical applied SQL migration or its checksums.

## Evidence and limitations

- Sixteen selected exact-source test bodies passed in an isolated JavaScript harness with mocked authorization, billing, crypto and providers. Seven changed JS files passed syntax parsing earlier; route-level Express/Supertest and real Node/Mocha suites are **not** proven.
- Latest branch head: `832ef8c75781d6c536a8b20f8f55800aa0bef805`. Mandatory checks on this final SHA must be completed; prior green statuses are not transferable.
- Required before any merge: `pnpm exec mocha tests/a-campaign-sends-only-to-who-was-authorised.test.js tests/a-remainder-send-refuses-what-it-cannot-know.test.js tests/an-owner-told-a-hundred-were-missed-can-find-out-which.test.js tests/the-send-route-reaches-only-the-consented.test.js`, full CI and browser matrix, clean native migrations/RLS, provider-free staging Resend mocks and owner-approved reconciliation proof.
- **A separate durable provider-authoritative reconciliation/adjudication workflow is still missing**. The unknown-send safety gate will intentionally block a remainder until that evidence can be recorded.

## Release safeguards

Draft only and independent of #508, #509, #511 and #512. No live emails, credits, money actions, migration apply, production activation, deployment or merge. Do not bypass CI, policy drift checks, tenant authorization, payment verification, review or rollback gates.

records.head: fix/unknown-write-outcome-errors-20261008
records.source_body:
## Cross-studio failure-truthfulness hardening (draft)

The centralized Express 4 error boundary can receive a failure **after** an earlier write or external side effect. The previous API 500 response asserted, verbatim, "Nothing was changed by the part that failed." That is not inferable from an exception and can encourage duplicate retries of payments, orders, publications, campaigns, or job requests.

### Changes
- Generic JSON 500 response now states that the request outcome could not be confirmed and advises checking status before retrying.
- Default HTML error response and the actual server HTML fallback use the same uncertainty-aware wording.
- No error body, stack, payment token, route implementation or customer record is disclosed.
- Add a real Express/Supertest regression probe to the existing `tests/a-failing-route-answers-instead-of-hanging.test.js`: a POST performs a successful in-memory side effect, then rejects. The 500 must not assert a rollback or leak the exception.
- No new Mocha file, dependency, API route in production, database schema, payment adapter, or side-effect/retry behavior changed.

### Evidence
- All three changed JS files parsed successfully.
- An isolated execution of the actual error boundary proved the counterexample: 1 write completed, HTTP 500 returned, final response explicitly said outcome unconfirmed and did not expose the internal error. **Not full Node/Mocha or hosted CI.**

### Research / reason
Stripe's idempotency guidance says operations can succeed even when the response is lost. Retrying writes should reuse a stable idempotency key and/or reconcile an authoritative receipt; HTTP 500 alone is not a rollback receipt.
- https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency
- https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- https://cloud.google.com/discover/idempotency

### Release constraints
Full exact-head `pnpm exec mocha tests/a-failing-route-answers-instead-of-hanging.test.js tests/the-route-error-log-does-not-print-the-key.test.js`, all CI/Node/browser/replay/security checks, route/inventory generation and independent review remain mandatory. This does not itself implement exactly-once commerce or automatically retry anything. Follow P0 governance issue #460. No merge, production deploy, provider credentials, SQL migration, money movement or website activation.

records.title: fix(telemetry): prevent tenant identifiers and unbounded HTTP labels
records.head: fix/http-telemetry-route-cardinality-20261008
records.source_body:
## Engineering finding: high-cardinality and private HTTP labels on all SONARA studios

**Reproduced at exact current main SHA `9d141e68d1ec14c037f92d1eebb3c2718d583c0a`:** `lib/sonara-observability.cjs` built OpenTelemetry `http.route` and SONARA's structured `http.request.detail.route` as `req.baseUrl + req.route.path`. Express 4 documents `req.baseUrl` as the **concrete matched URL** rather than the mount pattern. For dynamic tenant-mounted routers, this can expose customer identifiers to telemetry and create unbounded metric series.

### Patch
- `safeRouteTemplate` now uses the registered `req.route.path` template alone, with constant `unmatched` fallback. No raw `req.baseUrl` / `req.originalUrl` enters route metrics.
- Normalize unrecognized HTTP method strings to `_OTHER` per OpenTelemetry; preserve known verbs. Applies to both HTTP request counter and duration histogram labels.
- Add three regressions in existing `tests/observability.test.js`: pure dynamic mounted route, actual Express Router integration and structured event redaction, and bounded method labels. No new Mocha test file.
- Add `docs/research/2026-10-08-sonara-http-route-cardinality-and-privacy.md` with scope, cardinality math, the intentional loss of router mount-prefix specificity, follow-up registry plan, and production evidence requirements.

### Evidence / limits
- Reproduced source before/after with a synthetic tenant-mounted request: baseline `/organizations/customer-73958/jobs/:jobId`; patched `/jobs/:jobId`.
- Executed exact patched middleware source in isolated V8 with mocked OpenTelemetry counters, histograms and structured logging; both labels and event lacked the tenant identifier. Unrecognized method normalized `_OTHER`, known `POST` unchanged.
- Both changed JS sources passed syntax parsing. **The actual Node/Express/Supertest regression cases and hosted CI are not yet verified.**
- This is a privacy-preserving tradeoff: different mounted router routes with the same child template may aggregate into one label until static mount pattern provenance is available. Do not reintroduce `req.baseUrl` to fix that.

### Official sources
- Express 4: https://expressjs.com/en/4x/api/application/
- OpenTelemetry HTTP metrics: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-metrics/
- OpenTelemetry HTTP spans: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-spans/

### Release boundary
Require `pnpm exec mocha tests/observability.test.js`, exact-head full Node/CI/browser/security/native SQL matrix, metric backend sanity checks and independent review. Production site remains offline per owner direction. No merge, deploy, Auth/RLS migration, customer data, billing, provider credentials or release control changes.

- Exact-head CI reached execution: Node 24 and SONARA Industries CI failed lint on one unused `version` test variable. Removed without weakening any tests.

- Docker Image CI passed at the preceding head; this is not proof for the updated commit.
- No policy/grant/migration applied to any database. No merge/deployment authorization. Full exact-head CI and browser verification remain release blockers.

## Phase 10: Exact-head asset-version regression repair
- Inspected completed SONARA One Validation logs at earlier head: 7,114 passed, one asset-version test failed because `server.js` contained an obsolete versioned URL in a comment.

## Phase 11: Immutable public-asset cache bust

- Confirmed that the server applies one-year `immutable` caching to versioned public assets, while recently modified JS/CSS still had the previous v24 query token.
- Advanced the canonical version to `sonara-ui-20261009-v25-cross-device` in the HTML page frame, service worker CACHE_NAME/precache URLs, font asset URLs and cross-device regression assertions in one atomic commit.
- Isolated exact-source checks at commit `b0ea0afc1f41ab83740eafe2075edc38cedf8560`: **13/13** cross-device, **17/17** worker, **6/6** asset-version tests; **not** full Mocha/Playwright/Node CI.
- No changes to production, DB, RLS, billing or provider credentials. Keep draft until exact-head CI, browser/PWA version-migration and release approval are complete.

## Phase 12: Exact RLS baseline reconciliation

- Root cause: previously guarded P1 rollback-only replay required 25 legacy policy definitions. Read-only `pg_policies` inspection of the connected PostgreSQL 17 preview found **all 25 already hardened**, with 21 role-scoped `service_role` policies and 4 ownership-scoped `authenticated` policies.
- Updated `tests/sql/p1-rls-initplan-policy-dedup-rollback.sql` so **only a complete exact 25-policy legacy baseline** executes the original 25 conditional InitPlan ALTERs. **Only a complete exact already-hardened baseline** leaves those policies intact. Mixed, missing, broadened or otherwise changed policies fail closed.

This tests the comparison logic against metadata, **not** the full native migration replay or real-tenant adversarial behavior.
- No database SQL execution that changed schema or data, no RLS migration, and no deployment. Native PostgreSQL 16/17/18 matrix is newly queued at this exact head. PR remains draft until green CI, tenant-isolation proof and release approval.

## Phase 13: Public-only CacheStorage and root-asset allowlist

- Restricted worker interception for root-level JS/CSS/SVG assets to explicitly enumerated shipped public assets; unknown root file-like endpoints pass to the network untouched.
- CacheStorage writes require an explicit `Cache-Control: public` response directive. Rejected: absent public policy, `private`, `no-store`, `no-cache`, `must-revalidate`, `Vary: Cookie`, `Vary: Authorization`, and `Set-Cookie`. Public source asset MIME and redirect checks remain mandatory.
- Preserved strict core offline installation rollback. Rotated worker/frame/fonts/contract token to `sonara-ui-20261009-v26-public-cache-boundary` to isolate the new worker from the previous cache.
- Source-level checks on exact head: **19/19** worker, **6/6** asset-version, **13/13** cross-device (38 total) in isolated execution harnesses. These are not the full GitHub Mocha/Playwright/browser tests.
- No migrations, tenant grants, payment changes, merge or production deployment. Exact-head CI and real-browser offline/tenant cache tests are mandatory before release.

- Found an exact-head contract mismatch introduced by the Phase 13 worker hardening: `tests/pwa-contract.test.js` still asserted a retired `private|no-store` string, even though the production worker now uses a positive `Cache-Control: public` directive check plus identity-varying response exclusions.

- Independent exact-head isolated tests: **19/19** worker decisions and **3/3** non-HTTP PWA route, HTTPS registration and cache-policy source tests passed. PWA HTTP/Supertest tests, browser tests and complete GitHub CI were not run locally; the exact-head workflows remain required.
- No merge, production deployment, RLS change or customer data access authorized.

## Phase 15: PR-only workflow concurrency

- Reviewed GitHub Actions: PR #539 had 12 queued/pending exact-head workflows, and repository-wide Actions history showed many queued runs. Runner/billing capacity remains unverified; do not claim concurrency controls resolve the platform queue.
- Added workflow-level concurrency to six previously unbounded workflows: SONARA Industries CI, Native migration replay, Node Runtime Compatibility, dependency-scan, Docker Image CI, and Diagnose unresolved release gates.

New PR heads can supersede stale revisions of the *same workflow and same PR*, but do not cancel unrelated workflows, main pushes or manual release evidence.
- Added `tests/ci-pr-concurrency.test.js`: six isolated source-contract cases passed before commit, plus `docs/audits/CI_PR_CONCURRENCY_2026-10-09.md` documenting verification requirements.
- Preserved mandatory check names, matrices, triggers, auth/security policies and deployment controls. This commit does not establish full GitHub Actions CI success. PR remains draft and production unchanged.

## Phase 15: Real-browser service-worker cache boundary regression

- Added a **real Chromium Playwright browser** regression to the existing `browser-tests/public-experience.spec.js` suite. Creates a fresh browser context, plants a synthetic retired release cache, installs the shipped `/sw.js`, checks that activation removes the retired namespace, and verifies the new public cache includes `/offline` and `/sonara-one.js`.

- Transitions the controlled tab offline and back, asserting that public navigation displays the anonymous offline fallback and normal `/pricing` returns HTTP 200 after recovery.
- Scoped the native service-worker lifecycle test to Chromium because Playwright officially limits its service-worker inspection support to Chromium. Existing Firefox/WebKit browser tests are unchanged.

**Status: dependent draft PR, not deployed.** This PR targets `feature/autonomic-diagnostics-2026-10-08` (draft PR #510) and must not be merged or activated until that foundation is merged and proven.

- `service_role`-only `sonara_autonomic_execution_permitted(job, claim, fence)`: requires the real DB job to be started, unexpired, properly fenced, in the optional retry lane, and subject to global and resource-specific approval.
- `sonara-postgres-operator-gate.cjs` denies execution on a missing/invalid claim, absent or non-true DB response, or SQL/RPC failure.
- `sonara-controlled-recovery-execution.cjs` composes the operator gate directly into the server worker, ignoring arbitrary `isPaused` callbacks supplied by callers.

The PR includes its own Mocha-style regression tests, but **full repository tests and the native PostgreSQL fixture have not yet been verified passing**. The local container has no PostgreSQL binaries. Source module syntax passed local Node check.

### Constraints
- Distinct requester/approver text is a guardrail, **not proof of two authenticated humans**. A separate reviewed approval and audit admin flow is mandatory before activation.
- Operator revocation cannot retroactively cancel a provider effect already dispatched. Provider-side idempotency and fencing remain mandatory.
- No live job, provider, listener, timer, tenant, migration or production workflow is activated by these commits.
- Excludes billing, security, auth, identity, deployments, destructive changes and regulated operations from automatic execution.

Merge/reconcile PR #510, pass exact-head GitHub CI and native PostgreSQL replay, verify grants/RLS on the correct Supabase project, implement authenticated and audited approval issuance, prove real provider idempotency/fencing, require explicit operator authorization and a monitored one-tenant canary.

records.title: Harden customer automations with durable weighted budgets and approval composition
records.head: codex/customer-control-hardening-20261008
records.source_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up hardening for SONARA's low-budget, fee-only/no-custody launch model and customer automation governance.

This PR does **not** enable customer-money custody, escrow, wallets, autonomous refunds, autonomous publishing, or production automations.

## Engineering changes

### Governed customer automations
- composes tenant/role authorization, trusted server time, per-run customer/owner approval, weighted cost, daily/token budgets, concurrency, verified residual risk, and proof packets
- sensitive actions remain approval-per-run
- critical verified residual risk stays on the manual path
- review publication requires a complete customer-attributable proof packet
- no preflight result grants runtime permission or executes a side effect

### Durable resource budgets
- adds a service-only Postgres weighted budget store
- SHA-256 subject buckets: no raw IP/email identifiers in persistent budget keys
- weighted token refill plus a distinct daily-unit ceiling
- idempotent expiring concurrency leases instead of a fragile active-run counter
- lease expiry self-recovers capacity after worker/process failure
- application adapter fails closed when durable shared state is unavailable
- concurrency is acquired before budget consumption; budget denial releases the lease
- cleanup failure is explicit and still self-recovers on lease expiry

### Fee-only / no-custody invariant
- scans executable lib/routes code after comment stripping
- fails release if runtime introduces:
  - Stripe application_fee_amount
  - transfer_data destination routing
  - on_behalf_of
  - source_transaction
  - Stripe Transfers API routing
  - Stripe Payouts API routing
- keeps SONARA's own subscription billing separate from customer merchant funds

### Research / architecture
- updates NIST AI governance, FTC review, C2PA provenance, FinCEN payment-processor and Stripe Connect boundary research
- preserves the rule that provenance/hash evidence is not truth evidence
- preserves the rule that external-only is the cheapest/lowest-custody bootstrap posture, not a legal safe harbor

## Verification performed before CI

Focused isolated checks:
- automation governance: 21 passing
- durable budget adapter: 13 passing
- migration contract: 6 passing
- total: **40 passing / 0 failing**

The new no-custody runtime tree scan is syntax-checked and backed by repository searches; its full-tree execution is intentionally left to exact-head Node CI.

## Required before merge

- PostgreSQL migration replay green
- full Node suite green on required versions
- no-custody runtime invariant green
- security / CodeQL / dependency gates green
- generated contracts/docs green
- no regression to external_only default
- no production deployment from this draft PR

## Summary: P0 canonical origin and external payment return hardening

SONARA Industries and all three child products share OAuth, customer-facing links and billing infrastructure. Previous server code could construct outward-facing URLs from request-controlled forwarded host/protocol headers when canonical configuration was missing. Optional Stripe checkout return overrides were checked for basic HTTP URL validity, but not required to remain on the authorized SONARA origin.

### Implemented (draft; NOT shipped)
- `lib/sonara-site-origin.cjs`: accept a configured HTTPS origin only; fail closed on missing/invalid configuration in production and all Vercel environments, even if `NODE_ENV` is misconfigured. Do not use forwarded headers for hosted URLs.
- `server.js`: reuse one canonical origin factory; refuse to open billing portal sessions without the verified public origin.
- `lib/sonara-billing.cjs`: verify canonical URL and **both** success/cancel overrides are exactly same-origin, same-protocol, and free of credentials/fragments. Reject unsafe values **before Stripe Price lookup or Checkout session POST**. Return `site_origin_not_configured` or `checkout_redirect_untrusted`, with refusal telemetry.
- Maintain HTTP loopback (`localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`) Checkout returns for **non-hosted local development only**; require HTTPS everywhere else.
- `lib/sonara-business-employee-invites.cjs`: refuse bearer invitation persistence and outbound email when canonical origin is absent.
- `tests/production-origin-must-not-follow-request-headers.test.js`: ten focused test cases cover forged headers, malformed/credentialed URL, bad redirects, missing configuration, provider no-write, local-loopback compatibility, hosted preview and shared URL factory wiring.
- `docs/security/SONARA_CANONICAL_ORIGIN_CHECKOUT_BOUNDARY_2026-10-08.md`: threat model, documentation/research, operator runbook and release acceptance checklist.

**Source-only verification performed:** JavaScript syntax compiled for the five touched runtime/test files and seven source contract assertions passed at the earlier branch revision. This is **not** hosted CI, real payment execution, live OAuth, or production evidence. Re-run syntax and checks on the final exact head.

### Merge/release requirements — all incomplete until evidence exists
- [ ] Focused Mocha suite and full `pnpm run verify:launch`, typecheck, security scanners green on exact head
- [ ] Existing billing, pricing, OAuth, invite and share-link regression suites green
- [ ] GitHub native migration replay, RLS and tenant-isolation gates remain green
- [ ] Two-site sandbox attempts demonstrate refusal for untrusted redirect or Host headers and success for valid configured SONARA site
- [ ] Independently inspect concurrent open security/platform PRs, especially #540 touching `server.js`
- [ ] Protect `main`, require independent review and enforce environment approvals
- [ ] Get separate owner authorization to restore website or deploy; confirm release SHA, real provider entitlement and rollback

**No** live Stripe charge or configuration, database migration, GitHub merge, Vercel deployment, mobile publication, site unpause or customer-data operation was performed.

Refs: OWASP Host Header Injection https://wstg.owasp.org/latest/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/07-Injection/17-Host_Header_Injection/ ; Stripe Session redirect contract https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/object

### Additional P0 billing status reliability (follow-on implementation)
- Hardened `getBillingPanelSummary()` for the parent and all three child-product billing screens: a malformed HTTP-200/PostgREST response cannot be read as no subscription.
- Explicit organization-scoped `status=in.(active,trialing)` lookup when bounded recent history has no active record, preventing older live subscriptions from being hidden by the last five updates.
- No paid entitlement is granted; missing or malformed data results in an honest unreadable status.
- Expanded `tests/a-billing-page-says-what-happens-next.test.js` with JSON shape/corruption, hidden-active-plan and second-read failure cases.
- **Isolated module execution** of eight representative billing-summary fixtures passed, including tenant-qualified URLs. This does not substitute for Mocha, CI or a real Stripe/Supabase sandbox.

## P0: Deterministic customer-cohort evidence, access and provenance

**Draft / NOT MERGED / NOT RELEASE APPROVED.** No production database mutations, paid subscriptions, role provisioning, deployments or website unpause in this PR.

### Latest engineering implementation (2026-10-09)
- Hardened `lib/sonara-cohort-roster-attestation.cjs`: the Ed25519-signed manifest SHA-256 must match the actual immutable source-evidence Buffer. A separate **trusted operator-pinned** `approvedSourceQuerySha256` is now mandatory and must match the manifest's `sourceQuerySha256`; a valid signature for an **unreviewed query** is rejected before any DB connection.
- Require compact unambiguous JSON encoding: parsed and reserialized JSON must match original signed/evidence bytes. This rejects duplicate keys and noncanonical JSON which might be interpreted differently by different signers/verifiers.
- Changed `lib/sonara-cohort-snapshot-reader.cjs` to pass the reviewed query hash through the pre-connect gate.
- Expanded `tests/cohort-snapshot-reader.test.js` to include valid signed manifest/query approvals and negative cases for missing/wrong query digest, duplicate approval keys, duplicate manifest keys and noncanonical encoding.
- Updated `docs/operations/CUSTOMER_COHORT_PROOF.md` with independent reviewed-query pinning, JSON canonicalization, key custody and honest replay limitations.

### Verification and current blockers
- **29/29** source-backed focused cohort/snapshot cases passed in a JavaScript compatibility harness with **simulated** cryptographic and Buffer primitives. This is NOT native Node/Mocha, real PostgreSQL, release CI, or signing-KMS verification.
- Prior real Node 22 smoke verified native Ed25519 and SHA-256 APIs only; full exact-source native tests remain pending.
- Native PostgreSQL 16/17/18 disposable replay fixture, two synthetic tenants, non-BYPASSRLS role, RLS mutation canary and test hook were implemented earlier; **real exact-head execution still pending**.
- Latest checks still queued across the repository; read-only GitHub API reports a substantial queued workflow backlog (698 queued workflows sampled at this pass). The reason for runner nonexecution has NOT been confirmed.
- A valid signed manifest is still an **issuer claim**, not proof that the organization population is complete or all user consent recorded.
- The signature is **reusable until expiration** for the exact signed scope; this version does not have a durable one-time nonce registry and must not claim strict replay prevention.
- `verifiedPaidConversionRate` intentionally remains null until signed Stripe invoices/events are reconciled to scoped active entitlements.

### Verified upstream blockers (log-based, 2026-10-09)
The unrelated CI-throughput branch [PR #559](https://github.com/famouslytrill-boop/sonara-os/pull/559) has completed jobs that supply actionable **baseline** failures, not proof against this PR head:
- Native PostgreSQL replay aborts at `P1 RLS initplan and policy-overlap guarded rollback proof`: **`P1 policy definition drift on 25 policies; abort`**. Our cohort SQL fixture is registered before that P1 stage but it still needs its own exact-head run and marker.
- SONARA Industries Mocha tests report **handoff 513 test files vs Mocha 516** on that branch. Regenerate via the repository's canonical generator and re-verify; do not forge counts.
- Source licence checker rejects `ios/README.md:7` for wording about open-source XcodeGen, a tooling licence that is not a SONARA source grant.
- Existing draft [PR #545](https://github.com/famouslytrill-boop/sonara-os/pull/545) separately fixes source-vs-live RLS replay policy lineage; [PR #547](https://github.com/famouslytrill-boop/sonara-os/pull/547) separately addresses the XcodeGen wording; [PR #559](https://github.com/famouslytrill-boop/sonara-os/pull/559) addresses CI runner occupancy. **Do not blindly cherry-pick or merge them while red**; each must pass independently before reconciliation.
- GitHub's read-only Actions API returned **698 queued workflow runs** repository-wide at inspection; the cause of all queued runs is not fully established. Stop needlessly resetting checks through small commits while waiting on exact-head evidence.

### Required release gates
1. Clear/diagnose CI workflow runner backlog without bypassing mandatory checks; run exact-head Node/Mocha, native PostgreSQL replay, RLS/security, generated docs, lint/typecheck and owner review.
2. Approve a fixed audited source-query hash, independent complete organization roster, retention/consent policy and signing KMS/key rotation. Never derive the pinned hash from a report request.
3. Stage a real non-BYPASSRLS reporting identity with two-tenant positive/negative policy proof and immutable transaction snapshot.
4. Separately prove live Stripe event signature + checkout/invoice/renewal/cancellation/refund → entitlement authorization/revocation before paid access.
5. Release only after controlled canary, audit, rollback and explicit owner approval.

References: https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html , https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html
