comments.body:
Second engineering pass completed on exact head `017907dcf53805a609221b00f15410756d12ef1d`.

### New finding corrected

The first motion implementation scoped `accelerometer=(self)` / `gyroscope=(self)` to `/settings/device-feedback`, but the global Permissions-Policy omitted both directives. That was not a true default deny: both directives default to `self`. A route-specific Permissions-Policy also replaces the earlier header, so Creator Generation's camera/microphone override could have silently restored default-self sensor eligibility by omission.

### Implemented

- Added `lib/sonara-permissions-policy.cjs` with complete named presets:
  - `default`: camera denied; mic/geolocation/payment same-origin; accelerometer/gyroscope denied.
  - `creator_generation`: camera/mic same-origin; accelerometer/gyroscope still denied.
  - `device_feedback`: camera denied; accelerometer/gyroscope same-origin.
- Global server header now uses the complete default preset.
- Route modules cannot use ad-hoc partial policy strings; a regression test scans server/routes for literal Permissions-Policy values.
- Added account-level `motion` to the existing `device_permission_grants` model rather than creating another consent table.
- Added additive migration `20261009235500_motion_is_an_account_device_permission.sql`; it grants nobody, verifies prior constraint vocabulary before replacement, and leaves no-row as off/not-asked.
- `/settings/device-feedback` re-reads the authenticated account decision:
  - granted -> scoped device-feedback sensor policy;
  - denied / never asked / unreadable -> global sensor-deny policy and disabled control.
- `POST /api/motion/events` re-reads that decision before sample normalization or persistence. Revocation after page load therefore still blocks the write.
- Motion writes are rate-limited to 12/minute per IP + signed-in subject.
- Updated subsystem truth: bounded foreground motion capture exists, while legacy `user_device_permissions`, route-tracking and voice-command tables remain schema-only/inert.
- Added/updated regression coverage for policy completeness, account permission semantics, migration vocabulary, browser no-auto-start behavior, server check ordering, revocation codes and rate limiting.

### Independent executable evidence

All 13 touched JS/runtime/test files parsed successfully in V8.

Executed account permission semantics directly:
- no row -> refused;
- denied -> refused;
- unreadable -> refused;
- granted -> allowed.

Executed the actual browser client source:
- account permission OFF: button disabled, 0 browser permission requests, 0 listeners, 0 network requests even when click handler is invoked;
- account permission ON: 0 activity on load; explicit click -> 1 browser permission request, 1 bounded listener, 1 listener stop, 1 aggregate POST;
- aggregate retained one-decimal quantization and missing fields remained null.

Migration source checks confirm:
- extends the existing capability constraint;
- creates no duplicate table;
- inserts no grant row;
- verifies all six earlier capabilities before idempotent return.

Research basis:
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/accelerometer
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Permissions-Policy/gyroscope
- https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-permissions-policy-1-20260922/
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DeviceMotionEvent/requestPermission_static

### Release status

Branch is **40 commits ahead / 0 behind main**, GitHub reports it mergeable, and the PR remains **draft**.

Full exact-head GitHub Actions are still queued (including Node compatibility, browser, Lighthouse, native migration replay, security scans, reliability smoke and controlled deployment dry run). This is therefore source/runtime evidence, **not a green release claim**. No production deployment or production database mutation was performed.

## DRAFT — governed adaptive learning, tested two-tenant RLS probe boundary

### Implemented, not activated
- **Opt-in adaptation proposals:** limited to deterministic, tenant/user/scope-consistent consent snapshots, aggregate evidence comparisons, Wilson-95 scores, review-only responses, and zero autonomous source edits/customer actions.
- **Predictive intelligence (offline):** seven-day seasonal baseline with rolling-origin historical evaluation, uncalibrated volume-shift heuristic, bounded workflow DAG, and request performance anomaly triage.
- **Trusted reader contracts:** injected identity/consent/governance and separately verified customer inspect/correct/delete controls; governance and consent before aggregate reads; consent and membership rechecked after access; source exceptions return generic refusal.
- **Strict user JWT/RLS read selection:** no service-role/secret fallback for future learning evidence; legacy routes unchanged. Supports a low-privilege publishable key. The read capability is an in-process branded identity, not a plain JSON authorization object.
- **NEW evidence-origin improvement:** a previously plain-Boolean `liveProof` could be forged to mint a branded capability. The new `createUserScopedRlsReadinessVerifier` requires two distinct tenants/users/JWTs and known seeded positive row fixtures, plus four **read-only probes**: A→A must read exactly row A, A→B must read zero, B→B exactly row B, B→A zero. Denial probes query by exact row ID with **no organization filter**, or they would not test RLS. Table grants/enabled RLS are checked through a separate trusted callback. Failures, empty positive fixtures, or provider exceptions block issuance.
- **NEW token binding and freshness:** proof is issued into a module-private WeakSet and bound to the exact tested caller access token via a private WeakMap. Strict selectors refuse copy/JSON copies, swapped tokens and proofs older than **15 minutes**. The user JWT stays out of ordinary JSON serialization but remains accessible to trusted in-process readers.
- **No production wiring:** callbacks remain injectable and **mocked in tests**. They must be independently backed by authenticated live Supabase calls and approved tenant fixtures before the system can be activated. A fabricated callback can still fake probes; this is no substitute for real staging/production evidence. The target `sonara_learning_aggregates` table has not been established as a deployed schema.

### Read-only connected Supabase findings (October 9, 2026)
- One active connected project found; 418 public-schema table summaries and 163 applied migration entries inspected.
- `sonara_learning_aggregates` **absent**.
- Security advisor: three WARN categories (one public extension; eight authenticated-callable security-definer functions; leaked-password protection disabled), plus one INFO category (66 RLS-on/no-policy objects). Not automatically remediated.
- This project is **not independently correlated to Vercel's production target**. No user records, SQL modifications, permissions, credentials or auth configuration were changed.

### Test evidence / release gates
- **46/46 focused policy + RLS selection tests passed in isolated JavaScript harness** over files fetched from this exact branch. This is not the repository's full Node24/pnpm/Mocha test run.
- Required external checks still **NOT VERIFIED GREEN**: pnpm audit, full lint, typecheck, tests, build, browser, security, migration replay, production/staging JWT and RLS allow/deny matrix, existing release and DB reconciliation.
- No merge, production migrations, automatic source generation/repair deployment, customer-habit collection or runtime activation.

### Next engineering process before release
1. Resolve GitHub Actions queue and obtain full exact-SHA CI green including Node24, tests, lint/typecheck/build, security and migration replay.
2. Independently identify the active Vercel production Supabase target and migration history; reconcile connected project without exposing secrets.
3. Review the existing advisor warnings. Prioritize the eight authenticated-callable security-definer functions and auth leaked-password protection using staged, evidence-backed remediation.
4. Create a **separately approved** learning-consent/aggregate data schema with narrowly scoped grants, proven two-tenant RLS positive/negative tests, real consent revocation, retention/correction/deletion endpoints and provenance.
5. Only after approval, wire authenticated, no-fallback read-only source adapters and test a one-tenant pilot.

**KEEP DRAFT. No deployment or migration without all mandatory gates and owner review.**

Full architecture, formulas, proof limitations and read-only findings: `docs/architecture/SONARA_GOVERNED_ADAPTIVE_LEARNING_2026_10_09.md`.

records.source_body:
## Scope
A non-networked, fail-closed benchmark validation module to prevent incomplete or stale publisher transcriptions from becoming false 'official top 50' claims, plus a deterministic, approval-only engineering idea scorecard and 21 negative/contract tests.

- Four named publisher ranking references: Fortune US, Fortune Europe, Fortune Global, Forbes real-time wealth
- Reject malformed/duplicate ranks, unsafe/mismatched source URLs, invalid dates, future observations, stale wealth snapshots
- Even a complete 1–50 transcription remains independently unverified and **cannot be labeled official** by this module
- Cost ceiling, owner, customer commitment, evidence and risk tags required before scoping-review-ready; regulated/financial/customer-affecting ideas go to specialist and owner review
- 50 curated mathematical/scientific formula concepts and a cross-industry applicability/research note

## Boundaries
No new provider, keys, database schema, web crawling, copyrighted data, billing, messaging, financial advice, customer UI, production activation, deployment or changes to existing mandatory CI gates. User input is not verified third-party data. A completed list is not a publication authorization.

## Review checklist
- [ ] Exact-head CI/test/lint/typecheck/build green
- [ ] Adversarial tests verified to fail on intentionally bad data
- [ ] Validate proposed new source registry against licensing/publication guidelines
- [ ] Review against existing SONARA market and formula registries to prevent duplication
- [ ] Do not deploy or merge while release gates remain unresolved

Created as **draft** pending review and CI evidence.

## Phase 2 hardening (2026-10-09)

- An apparently complete top-50 transcription with any rejected row now reports `invalid_transcription`.
- Publisher pages remain **default deny** for automated ingestion and full-list republication pending independent rights/terms review.
- Unknown, malformed or duplicated risk classifications fail closed to specialist + owner review, instead of treating an unrecognized tag as low impact.
- A supplied URL/customer count does not make an idea 'scoping ready': it returns `independent_validation_required`. Scores are advisory, never production authorization.
- Added a primary-source evidence matrix covering Fortune, Forbes, SBA, NIST (including final vs. draft SSDF) and USPTO invention/patent distinctions.

### Verification performed

- 14 / 14 targeted assertions passed in isolated V8 execution against the exact committed module and test file, with a simulated URL constructor. **Not** a Node/mocha, pnpm, repository CI or production pass.
- A mutation probe flipping `productionAuthorized` to `true` caused four tests to fail, confirming the negative gate is meaningful.
- Last inspected run: GitHub Actions check-runs were queued; no all-green evidence. Keep this pull request draft and do not merge/deploy or activate crawling.

## Phase 3: non-executing cross-source evidence audit

- Added `auditEvidencePacket` to reconcile claim IDs, supporting/contradictory observations, freshness and malformed evidence.
- Fail-closed results: `contradictions_found`, `unsupported_claims`, `stale_evidence`, `invalid_intake`, `no_evidence`, and `human_source_review_required`; nothing ever self-certifies independent verification.
- Hardened ranking text against formula-like, invisible and bidirectional spoofing; constrained evidence URLs to HTTPS, bounded length and non-local destinations. The module **never fetches** them.
- Added W3C PROV, NIST AI RMF and OWASP formula injection research with explicit rights/integrity limitations.
- **21/21 targeted assertions pass** in isolated V8 with a URL constructor shim (NOT Node/mocha/pnpm/full CI). Mutation probes show that disabling staleness or granting claim production authorization causes assertions to fail.
- No new routes, migrations, provider calls, scheduled ingestion, publication, payment mutation or production activation. **Keep draft and unmerged** until exact-head required checks and reviewer approval succeed.

## Phase 4 evidence and CI follow-through (2026-10-09)
- Expose source-host diversity as a *concentration signal*, never a claim of independently sourced evidence; repeated `www.` and bare-host citations count as one observed host.
- Require non-empty risk classification. Unknown and absent risk tags cannot be categorized safe for an engineering promotion decision.
- Poisoned ranking rows take precedence over source staleness so invalid observations cannot be concealed.
- Added primary-source references for W3C PROV-O, NIST's in-revision AI RMF, and OWASP's SSRF caveat. Current module performs **zero network requests**.
- **23/23 targeted V8 harness assertions passed**; deliberate regression mutations are detected. Node 24/mocha/pnpm CI and production validation remain unverified.
- CI diagnosis: inspected a real `SONARA Industries CI` workflow run; main and Supabase-preview jobs both remained queued. Runner availability/cause not established. Do not rerun, merge or deploy without executed required checks.


## Phase 5 — Research-to-formula planning (2026-10-09)

- Reuses `lib/sonara-formula-engine.cjs` canonical metadata for nine explicitly allowlisted planning topics (restaurant costing, inventory, operations, media), with no duplicate expression interpreter.
- New pure `planResearchFormulaEvaluation()` produces per-claim evidence status, existing formula name/expression/version/assumptions, and human-readable unit boundary; it **does not evaluate inputs**, fetch sources, grant publication rights or authorize a customer decision.
- Rejects mixed-claim citations, arbitrary customer input or extra plan parameters, stale/contradictory/invalid evidence, and unapproved fields in provenance receipts. Source URL, scoring and customer demands remain unverified.
- Added primary-source engineering notes from NIST uncertainty, OWASP input-validation, and W3C PROV-O; no compliance certification claimed.
- **30/30 targeted test cases passed** in an isolated V8 harness using the committed repository formula registry (40 executable formulas). This is **not** Node 24, pnpm/mocha, full CI, or live validation. Mutation probes verify fail-closed evaluation and receipt schema tests.
- Current PR remains draft pending actual exact-commit required CI. No merge, deployment, migration, research crawling or customer data action.

## Phase 6 — Multi-defect evidence review + release-queue diagnosis (2026-10-09)

- `inspectRanking` now rejects unapproved source-row fields and publishes a composite `issueCodes` array so corrupted/stale/incomplete results are all visible together. It labels dates `caller_supplied_unverified` rather than treating backdated user input as an attestation.
- `auditEvidencePacket` preserves simultaneous invalid-intake, contradictory, unsupported and stale findings; `planResearchFormulaEvaluation` propagates them as blocking reasons, with source verification, rights, measurement units and reviewer approval still mandatory.
- Rejects raw URL backslashes because WHATWG and non-WHATWG parsers can disagree; no external fetcher was added and this is **not** sufficient SSRF protection for networked operations.
- **34/34 isolated targeted V8 assertions passed** on exact committed source. Deliberate regression mutations for hidden stale issues and unauthorized customer use cause failures. **No full Node24/mocha/pnpm verification**.
- Confirmed both `ubuntu-latest` jobs in `.github/workflows/sonara-industries-ci.yml` remain queued, with no runner start evidence. Actions settings/entitlements and admin branch protection could not be read through the integration (403 on protection read). Public rulesets listing `[]` is **not** proof that main has no branch protection.
- Keep **draft/unmerged/undeployed**. Owner/admin must resolve run scheduling and branch governance before required exact-SHA checks can finish. See the new Phase 6 section in the research document for evidence and explicit next steps.

## Phase 7 — Read-only Actions queue diagnostics with native Node tests (2026-10-09)

- Added `lib/sonara-actions-queue-diagnostic.cjs`, `tests/sonara-actions-queue-diagnostic.test.js` and `scripts/report-actions-queue.cjs`. These form an **offline, read-only queue snapshot analyzer** (no secrets, API calls, workflow reruns, branch or payment changes).
- Tracks exact-SHA mismatch, success/failure/skipped/queued evidence, missing evidence, runner assignment, actual job starts, old queued **workflow** duration where timestamp exists, and future timestamp contradictions. It never conflates workflow age with per-job queue time or asserts the cause of runner delay.
- Never treats success-only check snapshots as production approval; branch protection, exact required-check coverage and owner permission remain independently unverified.
- **9/9 real Node 22.16.0 targeted test cases passed** using a synchronous `describe/it` driver. The committed module and test Git blobs match those executed under Node byte-for-byte. Standalone CLI also exercised with a sanitized fixture (exit code 1 for queued jobs). This is not Mocha in repo, production Node 24, or full CI.
- Updated docs with authorized admin snapshot schema, command, queue investigation and support escalation sequence. GitHub's Oct 5/7 Actions incidents were resolved according to status; there was no recorded Oct 9 incident, so SONARA's root cause remains **unknown**.
- This PR remains **draft, unmerged and undeployed** until substantive exact-head required checks actually run, the admin confirms branch protections, and an approved release is authorized.

## Phase 8 — Real release-signal bug fixed (2026-10-09)

- Fixed the **false-negative** queue diagnostic case where a successful check-run snapshot could coexist with a failed/cancelled/timed-out **workflow** or **job**, yet the analyzer overlooked those outcomes.
- Added complete unfinished-state handling for `requested`/`waiting`/`pending`, explicit missing-workflow and unknown-final-conclusion findings, plus `failed_workflows`/`failed_jobs` counters. No change to workflow triggers, permission settings or release approval.
- **14/14 native Node 22.16.0 tests passed** using Node's built-in test runner (not Mocha/full Node24 CI). A stale fixture initially failed and was corrected to require explicit completed-success outcomes. Exact tested source/test Git blob hashes match the committed files, and the offline CLI still blocks queued results.
- GitHub documentation confirms standard hosted runners for public repositories are free; this does **not** resolve queued jobs, whose origin is still unverified. Concurrency changes could cancel pending release checks and were not attempted.
- Remains **draft / unmerged / undeployed** until administrator-led issue #579 recovery, exact-head green checks, independent release governance and approval.

## Phase 9 — Repository Actions backlog diagnostics (October 9, 2026 ET)

- Extended `lib/sonara-actions-queue-diagnostic.cjs` to accept **optional** bounded repository-wide `queued` and `inProgress` counts and a maximum-200-run recent sample, reporting queue ratio, distinct commit heads, cancellations, and per-commit workflow fan-out. **This is informational; exact-head release gates are unchanged**.
- New tests keep unknown/malformed counts and overlarge samples out of trusted output, do not echo raw sample secrets, and do not claim any runner root cause.
- **17/17 native Node 22.16.0 tests passed**, including earlier check/workflow/job failures and new repository-load cases. Verified exact Git blob hashes match locally tested source/tests; CLI fixture still returns blocked exit code 1. Full Node 24/Mocha/pnpm/DB/security CI is not yet verified.
- GitHub observed: 697 queued / 2 in-progress repository workflow runs; latest 100 workflow runs contained 17 distinct commit head SHAs, 20 cancelled and 76 queued. **Not proof of a trigger storm or specific GitHub failure**; sampled count only, and the queue can change rapidly.
- Keep draft unmerged/undeployed, avoid redundant commit-triggered CI fan-out. Admin must inspect Runners active/queued counts, settings, account limitations, concurrency and issue #579 before any controlled merge or production release.

## Phase 10 — Workflow/job provenance hardening and exact-head queue matrix (October 9, 2026 ET)

- Fixed the offline diagnostic's lack of `job.run_id` to `workflow.id` association, plus optional job `head_sha` contradictions, invalid workflow identities and snapshots containing jobs from only a subset of workflows. `jobLinkage.completeJobInventoryVerified` deliberately stays false; at least one job per workflow is not proof of complete job pagination.
- **21/21 native Node.js 22.16.0 targeted tests pass** (four new association/coverage tests). The committed module and test hashes are byte-for-byte identical to the local Node-tested files. All three changed code/test/docs files were authored in **one Git commit** rather than triggering multiple GitHub CI batches.
- After commit `c361560f13a50ba13d012e30ac94e58063e54ece`, inspected all **11 matching Actions workflow runs** and each run's `/jobs?per_page=100` response: **54 jobs total, 54 returned**; **53 queued, 1 skipped, 0 runners assigned**. Earlier partial job coverage was correctly flagged; the fuller inspection does not certify build, security, migration or protected-branch success.
- **62 check runs remain queued and 2 skipped**. PR remains draft, unmerged and undeployed. Issue #579 is the administrative runner-recovery dependency; do not rerun storms, bypass blocking checks or restore production without an approved release.

## Phase 11 — Pagination-aware CI evidence and full direct GitHub cross-check (October 9, 2026 ET)

- Added optional, bounded `apiTotals: {checkRuns, workflowRuns, jobsByWorkflow:[{runId,totalCount}]}` to the offline queue diagnostic. It now identifies missing pages, excess/duplicate check and job records, mismatched workflow totals, missing identities and zero-record snapshots. These are **data completeness findings only**, not authority to release.
- **27/27 targeted tests passed with native Node 22.16.0 using node:test**, source and test Git blob hashes exactly match the committed versions: `1023e4a9613e3c50970d5c982e8fae8e4530bba2` and `9799bd905f04a1aff2e354f57cf1aa215ad9a480`. Syntax checks passed. This is not Node 24, pnpm/Mocha/full suite or real security/migration test evidence.
- On PR exact head `df0be570b6f8392ade8367e16d2fda8f6948caf1`, direct GitHub REST queries returned **64 check runs (62 queued, 2 skipped)**; **12 workflow runs**, including **two distinct `dependency-scan` run IDs**; and **63 workflow jobs** (62 queued, 1 skipped, **zero assigned runners**). Each `/jobs?per_page=100` response's `total_count` matched returned records. The diagnostic reported internally consistent counts and `unfinished_execution`, **never green**.
- The earlier workflow connector returned only **11** runs on the same SHA, omitting the additional `dependency-scan` run; direct `/actions/runs?head_sha=<SHA>&per_page=100` exposed it. This is why checking total counts/pagination matters, not proof that one duplicate-named run caused the backlog.
- The underlying runner/scheduler restriction is still unknown. Keep PR draft/unmerged, avoid additional CI-triggering commits and reruns, and require administrator-led issue #579 investigation, exact-head mandatory green CI and protected-main/owner approval before any staged deployment.

## Phase 12 — Cross-sector Research Atlas and 50-category taxonomy (October 9, 2026 ET)

- Added `docs/research/2026-10-09-sonara-cross-sector-research-atlas.md` documenting 15 sources, industry use cases, earlier 50 applied scientific formulas, sampling limitations and future implementation gates.
- One atomic commit on draft PR #605: `69fd4b654058121b7966405c81695777c6402eab`. Keep unmerged and undeployed while issue #579 runner scheduling, branch protection and full exact-head checks remain unresolved.

## Phase 13 — Fifty scientific formulas mapped to actual SONARA capabilities (2026-10-09 ET)

- Added `lib/sonara-research-formula-blueprints.cjs` with 50 reviewed **concept labels and explanatory expressions** for statistics, business economics, inventory, operations, manufacturing, finance, physics, engineering, information theory, media and reliability. This is structured research metadata, not a new execution engine.

No evaluation, users' data, scraping, advisor action or publication.

## Phase 14 — Unit-consistent custom Top-50 candidate evaluation (October 9, 2026 ET)

- Added `lib/sonara-research-comparable-top50.cjs` and `tests/sonara-research-comparable-top50.test.js`, documented in `docs/research/2026-10-09-sonara-comparable-top50-candidate-engine.md`.

### Implemented in GitHub source
- New `lib/sonara-social-preference-policy.cjs`: deterministic, side-effect-free mutation planner. Exact authenticated actor/owner precondition (still requires an independently real server session), expected revision, normalized keyword/topic/post IDs, bounded 200-item lists, duplicate/no-op protection, fail-closed storage and command whitelist.
- `set_discovery_opt_in(true)` is refused without independent version-bound consent evidence; false opt-out plans a revocation event. Account blocking, follows, age and country are **not** stored as user-editable fields.
- New `docs/sql-proposals/social-feed-viewer-preferences-cas.sql`: isolated/private schema, user-owned settings and consent event table, explicit Data API grants denial, RLS, security-invoker CAS function with row lock, expected revision and transactional consent auditing. **Proposal ONLY: no CLI migration or DB write.**
- 13 additional test cases added to the current free-social Mocha test file; no new tracked Mocha file or extra paid dependencies.
- Release guards updated: proprietary source count 429 → 430; test-only registry classifies new source explicitly, without permitting runtime activation.
- Extended architecture doc with current preview schema **read-only** findings and exact production/migration/RLS/consent/rollback prerequisites.

### Evidence
- Existing + new test cases evaluated with real source in isolated JavaScript harness (Node fs/path/assert shims, not the normal Mocha runner): **45/45 passed**, including 12 asynchronous tests inherited from Phase 2.
- Separately tested 14 policy edge cases and four post-hardening cases.
- Connected Supabase project yqncsonkxgwhcxedgevk is ACTIVE_HEALTHY **preview**, NOT independently verified production. Queried public schema *metadata only*. Existing public.user_preferences carries workspace_id so it should not be used directly as a universal personal privacy record.
- No PostgreSQL schema executed, no actual CAS/concurrency test, no native migration replay, no RLS two-user tests, no Node 24/pnpm/CodeQL/browser/CI completion and no production verification claimed.

### Security boundary
- The planner's verifiedActorId/consentEvidence fields are strict test seams, **not authentication**. Future caller must use current verified session and server-issued consent proof.
- service_role bypasses RLS; the proposed CAS function is only safe in approved server pathways, NOT a browser Data API RPC or blanket authorization. CAS does not constrain arbitrary holders of the service key. Private schema must remain outside exposed schemas.
- Report/block/moderation from draft #572/#573/#575 remain independently gated. A feed mute is not a reciprocal block.
- Site intentionally offline; **do not merge, deploy, apply proposal SQL, send notifications or enable feeds**.

### Before merge
1. Resolve branch stack #602 → #603 → this PR, keep separate exact-head CI and reviews.
2. Verify full Node 24 / Node 22 / Node 26 lanes as required, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, audit, typecheck, lint, tests, build, `verify:gates`, source count/allowlist checks.
3. Reconcile canonical Supabase production ID/history, generate numbered migration using CLI on isolated clone, run native PostgreSQL concurrency + RLS + privilege + audit rollback tests and database advisors.
4. Implement version-bound signed-in server adapter, user consent, export/deletion and authoritative block/follow read composition.
5. Only owner-approved, private one-tenant canary after all security and release checks pass.

The external research reference is the current Supabase RLS guidance, Google Play UGC rules and Apple Guideline 1.2; see docs for links.

### Follow-up security regression

- SHA-256 canonical content digest binds an attestation to the body, kind, source IDs, channel URL/state and timestamps: a source edit invalidates prior approval even if `updated_at` isn't advanced. **SHA-256 is not a signature or reviewer authority.** Future server loader must independently authenticate and revoke attestations.

Connected Supabase preview `yqncsonkxgwhcxedgevk` has public `growth_channels`, `growth_channel_posts`, `growth_channel_directory`, `growth_post_reports`, `creator_artist_profiles`, `creator_follows`. No non-internal update triggers exist on Growth posts/channels in inspected preview. Therefore a live public post IS NOT an eligible recommendation without additional independent clearance; `updated_at` alone is not reliable proof.

records.source_body:
## SONARA Social Phase 5 — two-authority, revocable, signed discovery evidence

**Stacked DRAFT onto PR #607 (then #606/#603/#602), with no route, live feature, migration, billing, client access or website activation.** Existing moderation/report/block draft #572/#573/#575 remains separately gated.

### Code actually committed
- `lib/sonara-review-attestation-verifier.cjs`: default-unmounted, server-port-based verification of **two role-separated Ed25519 signatures** over an explicit 21-field claim. Moderation and rights signatures have role + key ID domain separation; duplicate public keys across reviewer roles are forbidden.
- Checks: current versioned reviewer roster, approved policy version, strict field allowlist, key type/enabled state, canonical 64-byte signatures, source content SHA-256 binding (rechecked downstream by PR #607), signed AI/sponsor disclosures, age/territory scope and bounded ≤250 per-batch entries.
- Each read obtains fresh trusted key registry and authoritative hold/revocation snapshot, checks signed approval, then *rechecks both* before releasing approved claims. Changes return no items. Revoked signature IDs, signer keys and content holds exclude the post. Provider errors are redacted.
- Plugs into `createGrowthPublicProjectionSource` only through an independently reviewed server callback. This is **not a cryptographic credential issuer** and cannot verify the trustworthiness of an untrusted injected callback.
- 14 additional Mocha tests added to existing `tests/free-platform-surface-policy.test.js` (no new test file); exact source count 431→432; test-only classification recorded in release script. Extended architecture doc with authority, key custody, revocation, attack model and rollout gates.

### Verification and limitations
- **76/76** isolated JavaScript tests passed (33 async) using a deterministic ***noncryptographic*** crypto/FS shim; they exercise the full assembled policy logic but do **not** validate real Ed25519 handling in the module, full Mocha, Node24, pnpm or CI.
- Separate native Node **v22.16.0** Ed25519 API smoke passed 7/7 assertions, including two independent sign/verify, cross-role key substitution and post digest mutation. This standalone check is **not** a test of the actual GitHub module.
- No PostgreSQL replay, two-user RLS proof, actual reviewer service, key custody, trusted roster or durability proof. Zero customer writes and no runtime route/flags enabled.

### Security/provenance caveats
- A valid Ed25519 signature proves possession of the corresponding key, **not** actual content safety, legal rights, or independent reviewer judgment. Organizational separation of duties, production KMS/HSM key custody, reviewed human decisions and policy versioning must be established before any issuance. This is NOT C2PA certification.
- Blocking/reporting is not automatically solved by approval signatures; Apple and Google Play require live reporting, blocking, ongoing UGC moderation and user-facing contact/review systems.
- Revocation snapshots are double-read, but there remains a race between final read and delivery; a durable transaction/epoch gate and active moderation operations must be separately proven.
- Service-role Supabase reads bypass RLS. Approved source and reviewer adapters must use reviewed least-privilege credentials and maintain tenant A/B isolation.

### Next strict gates
1. Reconcile upstream stacked branches on approved SHA; protect main and obtain exact-head mandatory CI green, Node 22/24 suite, audit, lint, typecheck/build, integration checks, CodeQL.
2. Verify production Supabase identity/history. Prepare *isolated* numbered migration via current CLI for private reviewer/key registry, decision/appeal, content hold and signed attestation+revocation lifecycle.
3. Prove native Postgres key/role scope, concurrency race, rollback, cross-tenant denial, source mutation invalidation, signer suspension, and audited human-review decisions. Do NOT use raw user JWT user_metadata for authority.
4. Staff moderation/report/appeal and build responsive contact/report/block UI per Apple/Google Play. Verify policy/consent terms.
5. Connect approved adapters behind OFF flag with signed authenticated caller and rate limit. Conduct one approved tenant canary only after verified checks and separate controlled deployment authorization.

### Standards
- C2PA 2.4 cryptographic content binding vs signer trust: https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.4/specs/C2PA_Specification.html
- Apple UGC §1.2: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/
- Google Play UGC: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9876937
- Supabase RLS/docs: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security

records.source_body:
## Release-gate repair, isolated from product code

The native PostgreSQL replay currently aborts at "P1 policy definition drift on 25 policies" on exact-head PRs, including #609. The repository's last migration `20261008100000_tighten_service_role_rls_policies.sql` intentionally hardened 21 pure service-role policies to `TO service_role USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` and optimized four authenticated `auth.uid()` ownership checks. The old P1 temporary SQL probe was still expecting all 25 pre-hardening definitions and would attempt to rewrite them backwards.

This review-only fix:
- Checks all **25** policy names, commands, scope, permissiveness and exact post-hardening shapes; 21 must be role-scoped service_role/TRUE and four must retain the `user_id` owner comparison.
- Aborts on widened applicability, missing policies, legacy per-row `auth.role()` checks or a nonidentical subscription policy pair.
- Tests that dropping exactly one identical subscription SELECT policy is safe **inside a rolled-back transaction**, then verifies the original pair was restored.
- Corrects stale verifier commentary. **No migration, production SQL or customer records are changed.**

Requires the full native replay matrix (Node 22/24/26 and PostgreSQL 16/17/18), other mandatory CI, and exact SHA review. Keep DRAFT; do not merge/deploy/relax RLS checks simply to obtain green.

### Additional independent source-license gate repair
- `ios/README.md` now describes XcodeGen as an **external project generator**, not as a licence for SONARA source. Prior word choice triggered the proprietary-source scanner despite the repository remaining `UNLICENSED`; no source licence or proprietary protection changed.
- This addresses a second CI blocker observed on the baseline product PR. The WebKit browser regression and generated capability inventory remain independently gated and are **not** suppressed here.


### Follow-up evidence, not a green claim
- The initial post-hardening fixture passed its 25-policy audit but failed at the **subscriptions duplicate preflight** in native PostgreSQL replay. A diagnostic-only exception now prints the exact two source policy definitions on the next replay; it still fails closed.
- Read-only connected **preview** PostgreSQL 17.6 inspection found the two subscription SELECT policies currently identical there and service-role-only/ownership policies in their expected post-hardening shape. The preview connection is **not proven production** and cannot substitute for an independently replayed fresh database.
- Added byte-local generated-document reconciliation: 516 Mocha files on this branch and 59 formula definitions; replaced a source-licence scanner false-positive in iOS README without changing the licence.
- Latest exact-head full CI is still pending/incomplete. Branch protection, isolated production DB correlation, reversible RLS evidence and all-green CI remain required before promotion.


### October 10: source parity, synthetic RLS and browser harness
Fresh PostgreSQL replay has neither preview subscription policy, and early source migration 010 creates an org-scoped subscription table without user_id. Migration 011 uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and therefore does not repair the old table. The former fixture incorrectly attempted live-policy deduplication on the reconstructed table. The replacement asserts no such named source policies, then builds a rolled-back synthetic table, tests separate A/B/anonymous owner-read isolation, verifies deduplication does not widen access, and proves rollback removed the fixture. It is NOT proof that preview and source match. Source-parity audit: docs/audits/SONARA_SUBSCRIPTIONS_REPLAY_SOURCE_PARITY_2026_10_10.md. Browser harness no longer replaces the full document via page.setContent; it replaces only inert body markup to preserve head styles, origin and CSP for WebKit. Generated capability coverage includes activation_rate and retention_rate. All fixes require exact-head CI. The PR remains draft and no schema or production migration is authorized.

### Continued parity repair — source contracts and synthetic replay
Source migration replay has three distinct subscriptions policies (public membership-gated SELECT, service_role ALL, authenticated membership/admin SELECT). The connected Supabase preview catalog instead has two different user_id-owned SELECT policies. We now fail closed on any change to the exact three source policy definitions before exercising a separate synthetic two-user/anonymous duplicate-policy isolation test within ROLLBACK. Added audit detail distinguishing these histories and preserved browser test harness corrective work. No production DDL, schema migration, preview mutation, policy expansion or payment action. Exact-head CI is queued; don't treat static reasoning as a passing replay. Parallel PR #617 and #595 also touch this SQL, so resolve overlap by deliberate review rather than merging incompatible variants.

### Further engineering pass — CI artifact and browser diagnostics
Exact-head native PostgreSQL replay previously PASSED at SHA 62d013b355effdc8919d9eb8973abbbb8bb26cec; this is not a green claim for the new head. The last completed SONARA Industries CI failed because data/capability-inventory.json and/or docs/CAPABILITY_MAP.md are stale (node scripts/generate-capability-inventory.cjs --write is the prescribed regeneration). A failure-only workflow step now writes and uploads exactly those files for an engineer to review and commit; it **does not** turn the failed gate green or bypass any policy. The browser test's same-origin asset loader now records HTTP status, Content-Type, page origin and CSP violation details before raising, to separate actual 404/content-type issues from WebKit injection faults. Latest workflow runs remain queued and are not accepted. Production unchanged. The repository's other draft SQL repair PRs #595 and #617 overlap the same fixture; only one reviewed variant should be chosen.

### Browser quality progression — parser-loaded same-origin Creator fixture
A completed WebKit run on the earlier diagnostic head showed the Creator JS assets returned HTTP 200 and application/javascript while page.addScriptTag failed, with no captured CSP violation. The browser-only test harness now uses Playwright route.fetch() + route.fulfill({response,body}) to stage inert fixture HTML and explicitly whitelisted same-origin scripts in HTML parsing order during navigation, preserving original response security headers. Creator graph core, local device store and draft module are parser-loaded in sequence; the same approach covers local audio and image core fixtures. All scripts and HTTP MIME types are checked, and exported browser APIs are verified for relevant modules. No production runtime, app CSP, scripts, subscriptions or customer DB were changed. This differs from bypassCSP, which remains forbidden. Official basis: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-route . JavaScript source passed V8 syntax parsing; the new exact-head Chromium/Firefox/WebKit suite is still mandatory. Generated capability JSON drift remains a separate blocking gate; the CI artifact now contains exact regenerated files and no failure gate is disabled.

## Root causes verified on GitHub CI and connected Supabase preview

The old P1 SQL rehearsal expected pre-hardening text and failed on all 25 definitions. The new rehearsal compares **exact hardened roles, commands, USING and WITH CHECK** without ALTER POLICY.
2. Subsequent native replay failures were `subscriptions duplicate policy definitions drifted; abort`. **Neither** of the two extra `Users can view ... subscriptions` policies is created by checked-in migrations; the canonical `subscriptions_select_member` is defined by `011_sonara_saas_launch_system.sql`. Replaying migrations cannot prove two preview-only policies exist, and attempting their DROP during native replay is unsound.

## Implementation
- Assert exact hardened 25-policy catalog in staging; do not rewrite or grant anything.
- Assert the migration-defined `subscriptions_select_member` is PERMISSIVE SELECT for `authenticated` with the member/admin predicate and no WITH CHECK. Fail closed if either extra preview policy unexpectedly appears in native replay.
- No `CREATE/ALTER/DROP POLICY` in the fixture; it ends with `ROLLBACK`. The earlier P0 synthetic role/tenant read-write/deny test remains first.
- Add `scripts/sql/postgres-subscriptions-policy-reconciliation.sql` as **read-only** metadata-only review evidence. Actual connected preview result: 2 duplicate candidates, 2 identical exact shapes, 1 distinct effective definition. **No live schema changes or production identity assertion**.

- Read-only Supabase preview comparison: expected 25 hardening policies, 0 catalog mismatches, all 163 migration ledger entries including Oct 8 hardening migration.
- Preview subscription duplicate review: exactly 2 extra identical policies; these remain untouched. The preview's policy set is **not** assumed identical to native replay or production.
